finding.message: src/presentation/order.controller.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/order-read.repository.ts (persistence)

citation.quote:
Controllers may query read repositories directly.
The exception covers OrderReadRepository only; writes still go through the business layer.

exceptionClaim.scope: Presentation-layer controllers may import and query src/persistence/order-read.repository.ts (OrderReadRepository) directly for reads only; writes must still go through the business layer.

answer.explanation: OrderController in the presentation layer imports OrderReadRepository from the persistence layer at line 2 and injects it in its constructor (line 7). Its list() method calls reads.findSummaries() directly (line 15). This skips the business layer, and FF-S03 flags any presentation-to-persistence edge that bypasses the business tier. The code matches what the project says it intends. ADR-0004 is Accepted and decides that controllers may query read repositories directly. It limits this to OrderReadRepository and says writes still go through the business layer. Its Consequences section names this exact import. The controller follows that limit: the read path goes to OrderReadRepository, and the write path, place(), goes through OrderService (line 11). The rule cannot read ADRs, so it reports the skip anyway, and the verdict stays fixed.

exceptionClaim.scope: Presentation-layer controllers may import and query src/persistence/order-read.repository.ts (OrderReadRepository) directly, for reads only; writes must still go through the business layer.

answer.explanation: OrderController in the presentation layer imports OrderReadRepository from the persistence layer (src/presentation/order.controller.ts:2) and injects it through its constructor (line 7). It uses it only in list(), which returns order summaries straight from the repository (line 15). Writes still go through the business layer: place() delegates to OrderService.place (line 11). FF-S03 flags any presentation-to-persistence edge that skips the business layer, so this import fails the rule whatever the reason behind it. The graph shows the edge. The accepted ADR-0004 explains it: order listings are read-only and carry no business rule, so the project decided controllers may query read repositories directly. That exception covers OrderReadRepository only, and writes stay in the business layer. The code matches this: only the read path skips the business layer, and OrderService handles the write. The blocking verdict stands. The ADR makes this a deliberate, documented exception rather than an accidental layer leak, so the likely fix is to record the exception in the rule's configuration rather than to change the code.
